blogTitle: How High Should I Hang Apartment Wall Art?
videoTitle: How High Should I Hang Apartment Wall Art?
script:
How High Should I Hang Apartment Wall Art?

You know that feeling when you hammer a nail, step back… and immediately think 'that looks COMPLETELY wrong'?

Nine times out of ten the problem isn't the art — it's the HEIGHT… and there's actually a brilliant rule that fixes it.

The 57-inch rule comes from galleries — hang art so its CENTRE sits about 57 to 60 inches from the floor, right at average eye level.

It works beautifully on a bare wall, in a room with 9-foot ceilings, or with a single large statement piece — that's when you STICK to it.

[warmly] But above furniture? In low-ceiling flats? That's when you BREAK it — and honestly, that's where it gets interesting.

Low ceilings are the number one hanging headache in UK apartments — especially older conversions and modern new-builds…

With ceilings under 8.5 feet, drop your centre point down to about 54 to 56 inches — and choose art that's TALLER rather than wide.

Above a sofa or console, the BOTTOM edge of your art should sit 6 to 8 inches above the furniture — anchor to the furniture, not the floor.

Here's a little thing people miss — if your sofa is LOW-profile, your art needs to come down with it… or the whole thing looks like it's floating.

A little tip I love: for low-profile furniture, drop the art 2 to 4 inches lower than you think — then step back and trust what your eye tells you.

Gallery walls in small spaces? Treat the WHOLE group as one piece — its collective centre should still land at that 57-to-60-inch sweet spot.

[excited] And if you're renting and can't go nail-crazy? Adhesive strips, picture ledges, and leaning large frames are genuinely GREAT options.

Scale matters as much as height — your art should cover about TWO-THIRDS the width of whatever furniture sits beneath it, no more, no less.

These are great for a living room — a set of three framed prints fills that two-thirds rule beautifully and feels really considered.

Narrow hallway or open living area — the rules shift… in a hallway, go VERTICAL and keep art tighter to the wall at that lower centre point.

And in open living areas you have more breathing room — a wider arrangement or a single large piece can really anchor the WHOLE wall.

Room by room: in the bedroom, hang art so it relates to your BED — bottom edge about 6 to 8 inches above the headboard, right?

Something like this for a bedroom — honestly, one of my favourites… calm, masculine, really considered above a simple bed frame.

In the living room, anchor to your sofa — 57 to 60 inches centre from the floor if the wall is bare, 6 to 8 inches above the sofa if not.

[gently] The entryway is your first impression — keep art at eye level, go VERTICAL if the hallway is narrow, and keep it simple.

Okay — here's the actual step-by-step: measure 57 inches from the floor, mark it lightly with a pencil, THEN account for the hanging hardware distance.

Measure from the top of your frame down to the wire or hook — subtract that from 57 inches, and THAT'S where your nail goes. Simple.

For wall art styles — sets of three prints work brilliantly in apartments… they're flexible, easy to hang, and proportionally just RIGHT.

Something like this cherry blossom set — calm, beautiful, works in almost ANY apartment room… trust me, it's a crowd-pleaser.

[warmly] Once you understand these few rules — and when to let your eye override the tape measure — hanging art in your apartment genuinely becomes the EASY part.

Did you know styling your home doesn't have to be guesswork?

We've built a free set of Home Decor tools and styling guides…

From colour theory and design principles to gallery wall layouts and art sizing. Download them all from our site!

Find all you need to transform your home into a calming oasis!

Happy Decorating!
